rules.rule: Always anchor search terms on the annotated span itself. Never substitute or derive terms from surrounding clinical context (adjacent procedures, diagnoses, or section content). Surrounding context provides disambiguation only, not replacement terms.

Negated, normal, and absent findings → affirmative SNOMED concepts: (a) Negated ('non-X', 'no X') → positive equivalents: 'non-distended' → 'normal abdominal contour'. (b) Normal qualifiers (intact, WNL) → 'normal [structure/function] finding'; lab → 'within reference range'. (c) Absence phrases ('unremarkable') → 'no abnormality detected', 'normal finding'. (d) Physical-exam negatives ('without R/R/W', 'CTA without findings') → 'no rales rhonchi wheeze', 'clear to auscultation'. Never generate disorder concepts for absent or normal findings.

Lab spans → procedure concepts. Abbreviations: Hgb/Hbg/Hb → 'measurement of total hemoglobin concentration'; WBC → 'white blood cell count'; Plt → 'platelet count'; Na → 'serum sodium measurement'; K → 'potassium measurement'; Cr → 'creatinine measurement'; BUN → 'blood urea nitrogen measurement'; INR → 'INR measurement'; CBC → 'complete blood count'; BMP/CMP → 'metabolic panel'. Always generate 'measurement of [full analyte name]' alongside abbreviations.

Discharge instruction annotations: (a) Header span → 'discharge instruction', 'discharge education', 'inpatient visit with instructions at discharge'. (b) Education triggers ('educated', 'counseled', 'given instructions') → 'patient education', 'patient counseling'; drug imperatives ('continue X', 'MUST NOT STOP X') → 'recommendation to continue drug treatment', 'medication adherence instruction'. (c) 'Return to ED', 'go to ER if', 'seek emergency care if' → 'emergency treatment education', 'education about emergency signs'. Gold concepts are procedural acts.

Organ-system labels ('CARDIAC', 'RESPIRATORY', 'NEURO', 'GI', 'PULM') as standalone spans in physical exam, HPI, PMH, or ROS → generate 'examination of [full system]', '[system] physical examination', '[system] disorder'. When followed by 'work-up', 'evaluation', or 'assessment' → also '[system] investigation'. CARDIAC → also 'cardiovascular physical examination', 'disorder of cardiovascular system', 'heart structure'. 'Pulm' → 'examination of respiratory system'. Anchor on span label, not surrounding diagnoses.

Cardiovascular findings in physical exam: (a) Numeric pulse grades (1+, 2+, 3+) → combine with vessel name and laterality; 2+ = normal. Generate '[side] [vessel] pulse present', 'normal [vessel] pulse'. Never search grade alone. (b) Rhythm descriptors ('regular rhythm') → 'finding of regularity of heart rhythm', 'regular heart rhythm'. (c) 'Irregular rhythm'/'irregularly irregular' → 'irregular heart beat', 'irregularly irregular rhythm'. Do NOT generate disorder terms. Always include 'heart'; do not apply to family history.

In the Allergies section, listed items are allergens. Generate 'allergic reaction caused by [item]', '[item] allergy', 'hypersensitivity to [item]'. Do NOT generate only the substance name or administration procedures — the gold concept is an allergic reaction disorder, not the substance itself.

SNOMED-preferred forms for colloquialisms, misspellings, and synonyms: 'CVA' → 'stroke'; 'MI' → 'myocardial infarction'; 'CHF' → 'congestive heart failure'; 'ultrasound of [X]' → 'ultrasonography of [X]'; 'echo' → 'echocardiography'; 'body ache/aches' → 'generalized aches and pains'; 'bracheocephalic' (vascular context) → also 'brachial artery'; 'septic arthritis' → 'bacterial arthritis', 'infective arthritis', 'bacterial joint infection' (SNOMED: 'septic' in joint context = 'bacterial'). Always include SNOMED preferred synonym alongside colloquial form.

State and positional descriptors → SNOMED finding concepts, not procedures: (a) 'Anesthesia' as service/agent → 'under anesthesia', 'anesthetic finding'. 'Post-operative'/'postoperative' → 'postprocedural state finding', 'status post surgery'; prefer disorder terms in complication contexts. (b) Sustained rest posture ('lying in bed', 'sitting on couch', 'reclining') → 'recumbent position', 'semi-recumbent position', 'body position'. Do NOT default to sedentary lifestyle; target positional finding hierarchy.

Anatomical spans → SNOMED body-structure concepts: (a) Named structures → 'structure of [anatomy]'; generic terms ('tissue', 'fluid', 'wall') → 'body [term] structure'; joint movements in PE → performing structure; imaging landmarks → constituent bones. (b) Adjective-only spans ('facial', 'bilateral [body part]') → noun form; do NOT apply to noun spans ('graft', 'edema'). (c) 'groin' → 'inguinal region'; 'armpit' → 'axilla'; 'kneecap' → 'patella'. Laterality prefix → lateralized SNOMED form. Avoid functional substitutions.

Multi-component span annotation: (a) Single qualifier spans ('irregular', 'elevated', 'rapid') alone → extract nearest clinical entity: 'irregular heartbeat' near rhythm/rate. Partial table headers ('HEART') → infer full concept from adjacent headers: 'heart rate finding'. Never search qualifiers alone or generate body-structure terms for measurement headers. (b) Physical activity triggers ('short walks', 'climbing stairs', 'minimal exertion') → '[symptom] on exertion', 'exertional [symptom]'. (c) Sputum descriptors in productive cough context → 'productive cough with [descriptor] sputum'. Preserve trigger and symptom together.

'Leave', 'left', or departure verbs in narrative sections describing patient refusal of care (declining services, refusing prescriptions, 'CYA' language) → generate 'left against medical advice', 'against medical advice', 'AMA discharge', 'patient refusal'. Context of patient actively rejecting care overrides the literal verb meaning.

Patient state findings — context disambiguation: (a) Functional assessment headers → 'physical functional dependency', 'functional status', 'activity limitation'. (b) Diet tolerance → 'tolerating normal diet', 'tolerating diet'. (c) 'Drink' in danger-sign list → 'unable to drink', 'finding related to ability to drink'; no hydration procedures. (d) 'Drink'/'last drink' in alcohol history → 'drinking episode', 'alcohol drinking behavior'. (e) 'Sexual activity' in discharge instructions → 'finding relating to sexual activity', 'finding of frequency of sexual activity'.

Surgical specialty names ('Hand Surgery', 'Orthopedics', 'Neurosurgery') in context of follow-up, outpatient visit, or consultation → generate 'referral to [specialty] service', 'referral to [specialty]', '[specialty] consultation referral'. The concept is the REFERRAL act, not the surgical procedure.

Radiology/imaging annotations in results sections: (a) Standalone modality qualifiers ('Portable', 'AP', 'PA', 'Lateral', 'Upright') → '[qualifier] plain X-ray', '[qualifier] radiograph'. Do NOT derive terms from adjacent non-imaging text. (b) 'Stranding' (fat stranding, pericholecystic) in imaging reports → 'fat stranding', 'edema', 'soft tissue edema', 'inflammatory change'. Do not use bare 'stranding' as SNOMED search term.

Procedure-verb annotations: (a) 'Instructions'/'instructed to'/'given instructions' for patient guidance → 'patient education', 'education procedure', 'recommendation to'. Map to education/recommendation procedures. (b) 'Worked up'/'workup'/'work-up'/'further workup' → 'evaluation procedure', 'diagnostic evaluation', 'clinical evaluation'. Do NOT generate education concepts for workup terms, nor scheduling/administrative concepts for instruction terms.

Skin and wound findings in exam or ROS: (a) 'Skin changes' or '[body site] changes' → 'skin appearance abnormal', 'abnormal skin appearance', 'skin finding'; include 'abnormal' in at least one term. (b) 'Yellowing of skin/eyes' → 'yellow discoloration of skin', 'yellow skin', AND 'jaundice'/'icterus'; include both color-description and diagnostic forms. (c) 'Clean dry and intact'/'CDI' at surgical sites → 'wound healing well', 'wound healing finding', 'healing wound'. Map CDI to wound-healing finding, not individual descriptors.

Pathology invasion qualifier spans ('venous', 'perineural', 'LVI', 'lymphovascular') within cancer PMH/history → generate '[type] invasion by tumor', 'venous large vessel invasion', 'tumor invasion finding', '[type] invasion present'. Do NOT substitute surrounding symptoms (melena, bleeding). Span text must dominate (R001 applies).

Pathogen-antigen lab result spans ('CRYPTOCOCCAL ANTIGEN', '[pathogen] ANTIGEN') → generate '[pathogen] species antigen assay', '[pathogen] antigen assay', 'detection of [pathogen] antigen'. For fungal pathogens also include 'fungal antigen assay'. Prefer assay/procedure form, not disorder.

Monitoring/management verb spans ('monitored', 'assessed', 'managed') → (a) ALWAYS generate 'monitoring procedure' as the FIRST generic term; (b) then specific: '[object] monitoring', '[object] assessment procedure'; (c) Target regime/therapy class, NOT finding ('monitoring status' is wrong hierarchy). Past-tense verbs = completed monitoring procedure.

Mobility aid device spans ('walker', 'cane', 'rollator', 'walking frame') in activity status or discharge context → generate 'zimmer frame', 'uses zimmer frame', 'walking frame', 'walking aid use', 'ambulatory with walking aid'. SNOMED preferred term for walker/walking frame is 'zimmer frame' — always include it.

Procedure colloquial/abbreviation mappings: (a) 'Cath' in vascular/cardiac context → 'cardiac catheterization', 'coronary catheterization', 'catheterization of heart'. Derive terms from annotated span only (R001 applies). (b) 'Funduscopic exam', 'fundus examination', 'ophthalmoscopic exam' → primary term 'ophthalmoscopy'; also 'direct ophthalmoscopy', 'examination of optic fundus', 'retinal examination'. SNOMED preferred is 'ophthalmoscopy', not 'fundus examination'. Apply in any section.

'Graft' span in physical exam when context includes 'thrill', 'bruit', upper-extremity vascular description, or renal/dialysis reference → generate 'arteriovenous graft', 'AV graft', 'vascular access graft', 'hemodialysis graft'. Use 'transplant structure' ONLY when a specific transplanted organ is explicitly named. Prioritise morphologic abnormality hierarchy.

State and resolution qualifier spans: (a) Oncology/treatment context ('remission', 'relapse', 'recurrence'): combine with disease type: '[cancer type] in remission', 'acute leukemia in remission', 'disease in remission', 'clinical remission'. (b) General improvement phrases ('[symptom] improved', 'resolved', 'better'): generate 'resolution of [symptom]', 'improvement of [symptom]', '[symptom] absent', 'sensation of [symptom] reduced'. Always combine entity with state qualifier; never generate bare symptom name alone.

Drug/medication spans in clinical context: (a) Drug name in recommendation/instruction context → also generate 'administration of [drug class]', 'drug administration', 'administration of drug or medicament'. E.g., 'Tylenol' → 'administration of analgesic'; retain drug name terms alongside. (b) Route-of-administration spans ('Oral', 'IV', 'PO', 'IM', 'SQ', 'SC', 'sublingual', 'topical') → 'administration via [full route name] route', '[route] route of administration'. Do NOT generate dosage-form terms; target administration route procedure, not formulation.

Generic categorical term generation: (a) Clinical condition/diagnosis spans ('thrombocytopenia', 'neuropathy') → also generate SNOMED disorder-preferred form: 'thrombocytopenic disorder', 'leukopenic disorder'; include base term and common descriptors ('low platelets'). (b) Single-word observation-property spans ('color', 'shape', 'texture', 'consistency') in HPI/exam → generate '[span] finding', 'finding of [span]' as categorical term alongside any context-specific terms.

Spans 'within normal limits', 'WNL', 'within reference range', 'normal range' in labs/results context → generate 'measurement finding within reference range', 'laboratory result within normal limits', 'result within reference range'. Do NOT generate modality-specific normals (e.g., 'ECG normal', 'hemoglobin within reference range') — keep terms generic and categorical.

Non-compliance/adherence spans ('non compliance', 'non-compliance', 'noncompliance', 'non-adherence') in medication/treatment context → generate 'drug compliance poor', 'medication non-compliance', 'poor drug compliance', 'non-adherence to medication', 'drugs total non-compliance'. Anchor to the medication domain; avoid generic 'noncompliance in general'.
